Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{4}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

The image of the bottom side of $Δ$ under the action of $T$ is a line segment. Which of the following statements are true regarding the image?

- The image makes the angle of $0$ with the positive $x$-axis.
- The image makes the angle of $\frac{\pi }{4}$ with the positive $x$-axis.
- One endpoint of the image is the origin $O$ of the $xy$-plane, and the other endpoint lies on the circle of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at $O.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Horizontal Segment Under a Polar Transformation
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14047173/assets/86a240b5c7c1fc945e12da274be7e9cac14c1b5a9add004d52d72390afb39aff.png)

     

Consider the rectangular region $\Delta$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
\Delta = \left\{ (u,v) \: :  \:  1 \le u \le 3, \:\: \dfrac{\pi}{4} \leq v \leq \dfrac{4\pi}{3} \right\},
$$

and the transformation $\mathbf T,$ given by

$$
\mathbf{T}:(u,v) \to (u \cos v, \, u \sin v).
$$

Determine the image of the top side of $\Delta$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}.$
examples.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $\Delta$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the top side.

For the top side, we have $v = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ and $1 \leq u \leq 3.$ 

Substituting $v = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})),\,1\le u\le 3.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a parametric equation of the line segment that makes an angle of $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ with the positive $x$-axis and whose endpoints lie on circles of radii $1$ and $3$ centered at $O,$ as shown below.

Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{4}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the left side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the left side.

For the left side, we have $u=0$ and $0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{4}.$ 

Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(0\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(0,\,0),\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, as shown below.
